extracted.intended_audience: national and local regulators, policy makers and regulatory agencies in Korea (and OECD member governments) responsible for enforcement, inspections, regulatory evaluation and SME regulatory policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and best-practice criteria for regulatory enforcement, inspection systems, risk-based approaches, ex-post evaluation, and SME-targeted regulatory measures, aimed at improving regulatory delivery and performance. Focused on Korea but based on OECD principles and international examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence based enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory enforcement and inspections should be evidence-based and measurement-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deciding what to inspect and how should be grounded on data and evidence, and results should be evaluated regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting compliance and enforcing rules should be left to market forces, private sector and civil society actions wherever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections and enforcement cannot be everywhere and address everything; there are many other ways to achieve regulations’ objectives. Use non-inspection approaches where feasible to reduce burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk focus and proportionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement needs to be risk-based and proportionate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The frequency of inspections and resources employed should be proportional to the level of risk; enforcement actions should aim at reducing the actual risk posed by infractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement should be based on 'responsive regulation' principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection and enforcement actions should be modulated depending on the profile and behaviour of specific businesses (e.g., more attention to repeat or risky offenders; lighter touch for compliant firms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long term vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments should adopt policies on regulatory enforcement and inspections with clear objectives and a long-term road-map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set institutional mechanisms and well-defined objectives to guide enforcement consistency and future planning rather than ad-hoc short-term responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-ordination and consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspection functions should be co-ordinated and, where needed, consolidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce duplication and overlaps to ensure better use of public resources, minimise burden on regulated subjects, and maximise effectiveness; strengthen co‑ordination across regional and sub-regional governments and between central agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Governance structures and HR policies for regulatory enforcement should support transparency, professionalism and results-oriented management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Execution of regulatory enforcement should be independent from political influence, and compliance-promotion efforts should be rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and communication technologies should be used to maximise risk-focus, co-ordination and information-sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ICTs to support optimal use of resources, information-sharing across agencies, and identify priorities for inspection and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and fair process
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments should ensure clarity of rules and process for enforcement and inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement needs to be coherent to organise legislation and inspections; publish and clearly articulate rights and obligations of officials and businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency and compliance should be promoted through appropriate instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use guidance, toolkits and checklists to promote compliance rather than relying solely on sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism of inspectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspectors should be trained and managed to ensure professionalism, integrity, consistency and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide substantial training covering technical and generic inspection skills and official guidelines for inspectors to help ensure consistency and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-based inspections (guiding principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: A risk-based inspection system focuses on individuals/facilities/enterprises producing or dealing with processes and products of greater risk and is a continuous process requiring improved intelligence and information management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broad risk assessment/analysis to concentrate resources where needed; quickly identify repeat violators and apply proportionate sanctions; focus on points in import/production/distribution chains that pose greatest risk; prioritise preventive rather than routine inspections; optimise inspector time and resources; minimise costs to individuals via improved sampling and concentration on high-risk items; promote mutual recognition/equivalence between trading partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a shared information system / central database
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a shared information system that collects relevant information on probability and impact of risks using data on compliance and inspection activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central database monitoring inspection and compliance activities can help map risks, improve local government consistency and efficiency, and provide regulated bodies a mechanism to monitor compliance; support evidence-based performance indicators and joint common goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use predictive analytics and open data for inspection prioritisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply analytical models/algorithms using past inspection results and other data to forecast likelihood of critical violations and prioritise inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Chicago's food-inspection forecasting used previous inspections, weather, and other departmental data to find critical violations earlier; aligns with risk focus, responsive regulation and information integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt tools that ensure consistency and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrate on mechanisms that work, have room for flexibility, and are long-term with clear objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide well-defined compliance/inspection/enforcement mechanisms and implementation guidance to avoid frequent re-working of procedures; draw on OECD Best Practice Principles for Regulatory Policy: Regulatory enforcement and inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate resources based on data and risk analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Further develop a risk-based approach to enforcement and inspections by allocating resources based on data and risk analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh risks on the basis of their impacts and probabilities; use risk analysis to decide what to inspect and how; ensure appropriate data on risk supports analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular intergovernmental coordination and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly discuss and co-ordinate across local governments and link local policies with national policies to ensure coherence in compliance, inspection and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborate to update and publish new regulations or reforms, keep them up-to-date, and consider how regulations complement other policy instruments to avoid confusion, duplication or overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary authority scheme for compliance (consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider introducing a primary authority scheme allowing businesses to form a partnership with a single local authority to provide reliable advice across councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary authorities provide guidance, advice and feedback, align corporate objectives with local regulations, target regulatory issues affecting local businesses; examples: UK Primary Authority (statutory scheme, register, agreed inspection plans, training, recognition of good practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement in occupational safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage representatives from the business sector (in addition to experts) to strengthen stakeholder engagement around occupational safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of labour, business and academia in deliberation committees improves the quality of occupational safety and health regulations and legislative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for coherent occupational safety and health policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish guidelines or a framework to guide occupational management systems and ensure coherent policies on Occupational Safety and Health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such frameworks help strengthen compliance with regulations and standards and improve occupational safety performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase enforcement human resources and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase the number of human resources mandated to enforce occupational safety and health regulations and improve their skills and capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit more regulatory enforcement staff where insufficient; accompany resource increases with cultural shift towards service-oriented compliance, skills to conduct risk assessment, provide informed compliance advice, and educate employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen compliance systems and programs for occupational safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure tools and incentives exist to encourage employers to adhere to standards and abate workplace risks and hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create consultation programs and training systems to assist businesses—particularly small businesses—to increase compliance, educate employers/workers on best practices and rights to a safe workplace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a risk strategy for occupational safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a risk strategy to understand core threats to safety, explain their importance, and identify ways to address them with limited resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include behaviourally-informed policies to empower, nudge or boost people's ability to be safe at work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply behaviourally-informed approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Use behaviourally-informed approaches (e.g., Behaviour-based Safety, incentives, competition, social norms, nudges, personalisation and timing) to enhance effectiveness of regulatory delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: BBS as proactive bottom-up approach with frontline engagement; incentives/competition (Western Cape pedometer/energy trials); social norms/shaming (UK antibiotic prescription letters); personalised messaging increased SME survey response (Ireland). These approaches can be cheap, executable and apply across risk strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory performance assessment tools: ex post evaluation, Cost-in Cost-out (CICO), sunset clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ex post evaluation, Cost-in, Cost-out mechanisms, and regulatory sunset clauses as core instruments to evaluate existing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex post evaluations measure actual impacts and fitness-for-purpose; CICO restricts cost increases of new/reinforced regulations by requiring offsetting abolitions/relaxations and cost‑benefit analysis; sunset clauses (review and sunset or outright sunset) with timeframes usually three years (max five) induce retrospective review and revision or repeal of regulations that do not serve intended purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic ex post evaluation strategy and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a strategy or system of ex post evaluation that looks at the overall impact of existing regulations and regularly publish planned evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish systematic, planned evaluation activities to improve transparency, accountability and stakeholder participation; currently there is no published calendar of regulations to be reviewed—publishing plans would structure evaluation activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate quality control in regulatory reduction initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate quality control systems when reducing regulations to avoid increasing regulatory burden through poorly designed reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure abolished regulations contribute positively to the sector/economy and do not produce 'less is more' problems by embedding quality checks in reduction initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure improvements in regulatory quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce clear and systematic criteria and metrics to guarantee regulations are meeting intended objectives and to demonstrate the added value of regulatory quality initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop metrics to show outcomes and measure the quality of regulatory processes and their impact on daily lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support evidence-based policymaking (public database and evaluation methodologies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen initiatives that support evidence-based policy making by setting up a public database monitoring KPIs and constructing robust yet implementable evaluation methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public databases to monitor development and outcomes of key performance indicators and apply robust evaluation methods to underpin ex post assessments and policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored Regulatory Approach for SMEs and micro-enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt tailored regulatory approaches for SMEs, including classification by average sales and exemptions/less burdensome regulations for micro-enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2015 Korea classifies SMEs by average sales (three-year average) with different ceilings by industry; micro-enterprises are defined by employee counts with sectoral variation; micro-enterprises (<10 full-time employees) are generally exempted from certain regulations for 3 years and other tailored reliefs should be considered to reduce regulatory burdens.
